properties.description: Re-calling a constructor does not erase what the design already knew (crates/reflow2-core/tests/constructors_preserve.rs) — 9 cases. THE COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE WHAT KEEP THE FIX FROM BEING A DIFFERENT BUG: a first call still writes schema defaults rather than inheriting, a named property is still overwritten, and an explicitly-passed optional still wins — so `merge` never became `first write wins` or `you may never change this back`. create_node and import_graph deliberately still REPLACE, because an import document is a complete statement of a node and merging there would resurrect properties it meant to omit.
properties.findings: WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: all 6 defect cases failed and all 3 counterweights passed. THE AUDIT, not the instance, is the finding: 16 of 18 public add_* helpers named a SUBSET of their node type's properties and wrote create-or-REPLACE, so re-calling one to revise a node reset every unnamed property to its schema default. add_interface lost 13 including `designation` (which contracts are published boundaries, req:key-interfaces); add_requirement lost `status`, which IS certainty (dec:certainty-derived), so rewording forged the user's signature in reverse; add_capability un-built a verified capability; add_artifact was BL-166 still reachable one call away, that fix having landed on link_artifact only. It survived BL-46 and BL-166 because it is INVISIBLE until a property has been moved off its default. It violated req:no-silent-fallback, accepted and priority CRITICAL.
properties.name: Re-calling a constructor does not erase what the design already knew
